physicalNotes: Radius 0.2114376 Jupiter radii from Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.549ag183M/abstract): 15,116.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0195 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): P 3.8266472 d

sources.phase: Morello et al. 2026 (2026MNRAS.549ag183M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MORELLO_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2458985.8831 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 4 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
